comments_text: Chemical modification: Chain A (shown) is connected with chain B (DIGKYCGYAHALN, amidated) via a disulfide bond. Trp is bromated at position 6 (6-bromotryptophan). Sequence analysis:APD analysis reveals that the sequence of chain A shows 45% similarity to Centrocin 2. Activity: the heavy chain is responsible for antibacterial activity as the light chain (B) was inactive (MIC > 100 uM). Active against planktonic C. glutamicum (MIC 0.78 uM), S. aureus (MIC 0.78 uM), E. coli #1 (MIC 0.1 uM), and P. aeruginosa (MIC 0.78 uM). Updated 7/2021; 11/2023; 5/2024
title: Novel Antimicrobial Peptides EeCentrocins 1, 2 and EeStrongylocin 2 from the Edible Sea Urchin Echinus esculentus Have 6-Br-Trp Post-Translational Modifications.

comments_text: Chemical modification: Chain A (shown) is connected with chain B (EVGKYCAVAHAIH, amidated) via a disulfide bond. In chain B, the N-terminal Q is pyroglutamic acid (Glp). Trp is bromated at position 6 (6-bromotryptophan). Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of chain A shows 46.8% similarity to EeCentrocin 1. Activity: Active against Gram+ B. subtilis (MIC 6.25 uM), C. glutamicum (MIC 0.78 uM), S. aureus (MIC 6.25 uM), S. epidermidis (MIC 3.13 uM), Gram- E. coli (MIC 1.56-6.25 uM), P. aeruginosa (MIC 0.78-6.25 uM), fungi A. pullulans (MIC 25 uM), C. albicans (MIC 50 uM), Cladosporium sp. (MIC 12.5 uM), Rhodotorula sp. (MIC 3.13 uM), and S. cerevisiae (MIC 12.5 uM). Updated 7/2021; 5/2024
title: Novel Antimicrobial Peptides EeCentrocins 1, 2 and EeStrongylocin 2 from the Edible Sea Urchin Echinus esculentus Have 6-Br-Trp Post-Translational Modifications.
